whatFailed: A read-only API token that is correctly authenticated but not permitted to create is refused with `error.name: "ForbiddenError"` (HTTP 403), while the error-handling doc reserves `ForbiddenError` for callers with missing or wrong credentials and `UnauthorizedError` for exactly this case, an authenticated caller without the permission.

docClaim.quote: The `UnauthorizedError` class is a specific error class used when a user doesn't have the proper role or permissions to perform a specific action, but has properly authenticated. [...] The `ForbiddenError` class is a specific error class used when a user either doesn't provide any or the correct authentication credentials.
docClaim.doc: docusaurus/docs/cms/error-handling.md (strapi/documentation), upstream lines 425 and 407; snapshot .truecourse/specs/sources/docs.strapi.io/cms/error-handling.md lines 331 and 317
docClaim.section: error-handling / Throwing errors / Default error classes

observed: Steps 2 and 3 pass: the read-only token lists /api/articles and fetches one document (200). Steps 4, 5 and 6 pass: POST, PUT and DELETE with the same token are refused 403 with body {"data":null,"error":{"status":403,"name":"ForbiddenError","message":"Forbidden","details":{}}}. Step 7 re-sends the create only to read the error class and gets the same ForbiddenError, not UnauthorizedError. server.stderr.txt is empty and nothing is logged for the refusals, so this is the deliberate authorization path, not a crash.
impact: Low direct user harm, the wire behavior is the HTTP-correct one. The harm is to backend developers: the docs teach the inverted convention, so custom controllers, policies and middlewares written from this page throw UnauthorizedError (401) for permission failures and ForbiddenError (403) for missing credentials, i.e. the opposite of what Strapi core itself emits and of RFC 7235. Clients that branch on error.name per the docs also branch wrong.

rootCause.explanation: The doc prose is inverted relative to Strapi's own class-to-status mapping and relative to how core uses the classes. `mapErrorsAndStatus` in services/errors.ts binds `errors.UnauthorizedError` to 401 and `errors.ForbiddenError` to 403, the standard HTTP meanings (401 = not authenticated, 403 = authenticated but refused). The classes themselves are in packages/core/utils/src/errors.ts lines 82-103 with default messages 'Forbidden access' and 'Unauthorized'. The refusal in this scenario comes from packages/core/admin/server/src/strategies/content-api-token.ts lines 77-99: `verify()` lets a READ_ONLY token through only when every route scope ends in `find`/`findOne` (line 11 `isReadScope`, lines 77-83), otherwise falls through to `throw new ForbiddenError()` on line 99. packages/core/core/src/services/server/compose-endpoint.ts lines 41-55 catches that and calls `ctx.forbidden()`, which is why the body carries the http-errors 403 shape (name 'ForbiddenError', message 'Forbidden' rather than the class default 'Forbidden access'). Every layer of the code is self-consistent and HTTP-correct; only the two sentences in error-handling.md describe the classes the wrong way round. The bad text lives in the separate strapi/documentation repo, not in the tested checkout.

notes: Only step 7 is red. Steps 2 to 6 confirm the api-tokens.md claim 'Read-only API tokens can only access the `find` and `findOne` functions' holds exactly: list and fetch pass 200, create, update and delete are all refused 403. The scenario yaml's own note frames step 7 as '403-where-401-belongs' and cites #9512/#18782; that framing needs refining. Those issues are about requests with NO credentials, where 401 would be right. Here a valid token was presented and 403 is the correct status. The mismatch is purely the name the docs attach to each class. Suggested doc fix (strapi/documentation, docusaurus/docs/cms/error-handling.md): swap the two descriptions so ForbiddenError reads 'the caller is authenticated but lacks the role or permission for this action (403)' and UnauthorizedError reads 'the caller provided no credentials or invalid credentials (401)', and state the HTTP status each class maps to, since packages/core/core/src/services/errors.ts is the authority and the page never mentions the mapping today. Worth noting for the doc author that PolicyError extends ForbiddenError (packages/core/utils/src/errors.ts:132), so the page's own advice to use PolicyError for a custom insufficient-permissions message already assumes the 403 reading, contradicting its ForbiddenError paragraph two lines earlier.
